topic.title: Why does Russia own a piece of land between Poland and Lithuania?
topic.map_answer: where Kaliningrad sits: the northern half of old East Prussia, given to the Soviet Union in 1945, left with Lithuania and Belarus between it and the rest of Russia when the Soviet Union's borders split in 1991

title: This piece of Russia doesn't touch Russia
description:
Kaliningrad is part of Russia, yet it sits alone on the Baltic between Poland and Lithuania. How did that happen?
One line across old East Prussia and one empire breaking up, told on the map, year by year.
Sources: City Population (Oct 2021). The characters are not advisers.
